open_points.subject: A21 security review after the changed A19 Required test 5
open_points.text: A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
open_points.question: After A19 Required test 5 added `+`, `%` and a space to the query-value case, what are the recorded outcomes of the reopened injection_interpreted_input, browser_boundary and files_artifacts reviews?
options: Review all three categories and record that their outcomes and references remain unchanged.
Review all three categories and change any outcome, reference or guarantee that the new query-encoding case invalidates.
open_points.default_guess: Reopen all three categories and record unchanged outcomes after confirming that literal plus, percent and space round-trip without changing the link structure.

witness.initial: A21 is closed by its latest recorded review of A19 Required tests 5–7.
events: The State 2 author changes A19 Required test 5 by adding `+`, `%` and a space to the query value.
A21 rule 2 requires the review to reopen.
No subsequent performed-review passage states the result of that reopening.
outcomes: A later agent treats the previous A21 outcome as still complete and proceeds.
A later agent treats A21 as reopened and blocks closure until the three categories are reviewed.
witness.observer: The State 2 gate and the release reviewer

open_points.subject: A19 query-value serialization
open_points.text:
a value in a link's query, holding also `?`,
   `#`, `/`, `=`, `+`, `%` and a space, read back from the link as that one whole value, the
   link's origin, path and other parameters unchanged
open_points.question: Which exact query serialization and decoding convention represents this value in the generated link?
options: RFC 3986-style percent encoding, including `%20` for the space, `%2B` for the literal plus and `%25` for the literal percent.
Form-style query encoding, using `+` for the space while encoding the literal plus as `%2B` and the literal percent as `%25`.
consequences: The raw href has a percent-encoded space and can use ordinary URI query decoding; generated snapshots and canonical URLs must use that spelling.
The raw href uses `+` for the space and requires form-query decoding; confusing the encoded space with the value's literal plus would violate the round trip.
open_points.requirement:
a value in a link's query, holding also `?`,
   `#`, `/`, `=`, `+`, `%` and a space, read back from the link as that one whole value, the
   link's origin, path and other parameters unchanged
open_points.default_guess: Use percent encoding with `%20` for space, `%2B` for plus and `%25` for percent.

open_points.subject: A19-1 and A19-2 witness check for query links
open_points.text:
a value in a link's query, holding also `?`,
   `#`, `/`, `=`, `+`, `%` and a space, read back from the link as that one whole value, the
   link's origin, path and other parameters unchanged
open_points.question: By what observation does the witness check establish that the value was read back whole and that the origin, path and other parameters were unchanged?
options: Parse the rendered link with an independent standards-compliant URL/query parser and compare the decoded parameter and every unaffected URL component.
Exercise the rendered link through a browser or equivalent end-to-end client and assert the value received at the destination together with the unchanged route and parameters.
consequences: The check is focused and deterministic but proves parser-level behavior rather than the complete browser-to-handler path.
The check covers browser and request parsing behavior but requires a larger integration fixture and a destination that exposes the received values.
open_points.requirement:
a value in a link's query, holding also `?`,
   `#`, `/`, `=`, `+`, `%` and a space, read back from the link as that one whole value, the
   link's origin, path and other parameters unchanged
open_points.default_guess: Use an independent URL parser in the renderer witness check, with an end-to-end case only if the assembly already provides one.
